title: JavaScript Language Quiz
description: Deep dive into JS prototypes, closures, V8 optimizations, and strict equality behavior.

questions.question: What will the following code output to the console?
questions.explanation: Because `var` is function-scoped rather than block-scoped, there is only one shared `i` variable in the outer scope. By the time the setTimeout callbacks run 10ms later, the loop has finished and `i` equals 3. Replacing `var` with block-scoped `let` creates a new binding for each iteration, which prints 0, 1, 2.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between `WeakMap` and standard `Map` in JavaScript?
options: WeakMap values are restricted to primitive numbers and booleans.
WeakMap keys must be objects or non-registered symbols, and they do not prevent their keys from being garbage-collected if no other references exist.
WeakMap cannot be accessed inside asynchronous functions.
WeakMap operates in O(N) lookup time while Map is O(1).
questions.explanation: In standard `Map`, holding an object as a key prevents that object from being garbage-collected even if no other references exist in the application. In `WeakMap`, object keys are held weakly; once the object has no external references, the entry is automatically freed by the garbage collector.
